purpose: why four EXECUTABLE models have no pair, quoted from their pinned code
method: static reading of the named file:line sites; no checkpoint load, no GPU

clvc_net.why: CLVC-Net is not one forward. The pinned evaluator drives TWO models and concatenates their features: `test.py:48` and `test.py:116` do `torch.cat([F.normalize(local_model.extract_img_feature(imgs)[1]), F.normalize(global_model.extract_img_feature(imgs)[1])], dim=1)` -> a 2048-d row from two 4096-d halves. The shared hook contract is `native_features(paths, texts)` on ONE network, so this needs a new hook shape (a two-model capture), not another ModelScope field.
clvc_net.loader: workbench/replay/clvc_net.py:125 `_load_replay_modules(source_root)` -> (torch, datasets, test_module) -- a 3-tuple with NO data_utils, so the shared `load_replay_modules()` index-2 `data_utils` read does not apply
clvc_net.dataset: workbench/third_party/CLVCNet/datasets.py:14 `__init__(path, split='train', existed_npy=True, transform=None)` -- no `noise_ratio`, and the keyword set differs from the LAVIS family
clvc_net.scope: per-category: `model_clvc_net.py:205 category_scopes = ('dress','shirt','toptee')`, three separate checkpoint files
clvc_net.also: the adapter's `score()` is cosine over concatenated per-half-normalised 2048-d rows, so the comparator's gallery layout differs from the 32x256 BLIP-2 layout
clvc_net.gpu_cost: unknown, but two models per forward and a 74k-image gallery makes a full-population encode the largest of the four

tme.why: `workbench/replay/tme.py:352-356` (the `raise` is at `:356`) refuses a category subset outright: 'The native evaluator always computes all three categories and has no single-category API. Refuse subsets rather than report metrics for categories the operator did not request.' A per-category pair — which is the shape every existing artifact uses — is therefore not expressible through this evaluator at all.
tme.dataset: `tme_data.FashioniqPath = str(dataset_root) + '/'` (`tme.py:365`), i.e. the evaluator reads the dataset through a module-level global rather than a handle
tme.also: needs LAVIS BLIP-2 `pretrain` weights staged as an external runtime asset
tme.gpu_cost: full three-category native evaluation in one process; the widest of the four

tgcir.why: `workbench/replay/tgcir.py:174 _load_tgcir(source_root, device)` returns `(torch, (clip, datasets, tg_test), adaptations)` -- 3 elements, and the middle is itself a 3-tuple. It also needs `clip.load('ViT-B/16')` PREPROCESS for the transform, not `data_utils.targetpad_transform(1.25, 224)`, so the shared transform/processor assumption is wrong for this model. The pinned source is CUDA-hard (`model.py:32,107,120,136,244,251`, `test.py:31,47,101,115`) with no device guard.
tgcir.loader: `workbench/replay/tgcir.py:174` -- see above; plus a torch-1.7 pickle alias patch (`_LinearWithBias`) applied at load
tgcir.also: the replay is a WORKBENCH-ADDED path over the pinned encoder; `test.py` has no CLI, so there is no author evaluator to be faithful to

ptha_mtst.why: `cirr_transfer` is a CIRR-trained -> FashionIQ transfer checkpoint, not a FashionIQ reproduction (`models.yaml reproduction_status: SELECTED_TRANSFER_ONLY`; the adapter's own status string says so). A G1/G2 pair measures adapter-vs-native AGREEMENT for the same checkpoint, which is meaningful, but the registry's own disposition for this model is `TRANSFER_ONLY`, so a pair here would be measuring a model the campaign does not treat as a FashionIQ configuration. That is a scope decision for the acceptance owner, not a producer gap.
ptha_mtst.loader: `workbench/replay/ptha_mtst.py` has no `_load_replay_modules`; it drives a subprocess-shaped official evaluator through `evaluate_transfer` (`:291`) and `preflight` (`:57`)
ptha_mtst.adapter: `model_ptha_mtst.py:360` `model.extract_target_features(batch, mode='mean', target_only=True)` -- a different target-side contract from the BLIP-2 32x256 layout
